svg.aria-label: flint-lite: consumer pods in any cluster mount a PVC whose PV points at the hub Service on port 2049; the node kernel NFS client carries the bytes; one hub pod serves NFSv4.2 from a PVC that holds the working set; the S3 prefix holds the durable copy, published and hydrated by the hub, with a control namespace holding the epoch, manifest and owner cells.

.flint/owner survives state loss
reserved: a client file here can never shadow it
Consumers never hold bucket credentials.
The bucket trusts exactly one principal — the hub.
Everyone else reaches the bytes through :2049,
which has no bucket credential to leak.
What the hub is for, and what it costs
It is the coherence authority
One process holds every lease, lock and open, so N pods
across N clusters see ONE tree. This is the only front end
of the three where two writers can share a directory live.
That authority is also the constraint: one pod, one replica,
Recreate. A second hub on the prefix would be split-brain,
which the epoch cell fences and the operator refuses up front.
One hub serves one prefix. Several volumes ⇒ several hubs.
S3 is the durability, and the RPO is the cadence
The PVC is a working set the hub flushes to the bucket on a
timer. Everything durable is in S3; everything fast is on disk.
A cold read hydrates from the bucket first, and both doors say
so rather than blocking forever: NFS parks the caller with
NFS4ERR_DELAY, HTTP answers 503 + Retry-After.
Losing the PVC is a rebuild. Losing the bucket is a loss.
Only one of those two is backed up, and it is not the disk.
The two doors are secured differently
:2049 is AUTH_SYS. The client asserts its own uid and the
server takes it, so POSIX modes are evaluated against a
SELF-DECLARED identity. Reachability is the real boundary.
:8080 can rewrite every file in the share, so it stays
ClusterIP-only, never joins the Service, and mounts no routes
at all without a bearer token — 404, not 401.
That token is per-SHARE, not per-user. See the identity page.
